moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
learningObjectives: Explain how the TestData - Expert Module consolidates Create, Find, Update, and more into a single module.
Choose documented Test data task options for item, type and lock operations.
Distinguish non-locking ReadOnly from explicit unlocking.
Configure a synthetic create, read, find and update workflow with the Expert Module.

elements.description: Combines operations offered by dedicated TestData modules and adds reading and lock-management tasks. It belongs to the Standard subset under Test Data Management → Test Data Service. Security-enabled installations may restrict operations by user group.

Select the operation through Test data task. Tosca 2026.1 LTS documents Create, ReadOnly, Find, Update, DeleteItem, DeleteType, DeleteAll, LockItem, UnlockItem, LockType and UnlockType. Check the module shipped with your installed version.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Choose the task and its scope

elements.title: What each function does
items: Create — adds an item to a specified existing or new type.
ReadOnly — reads an item without acquiring an exclusive lock.
Find — retrieves one item selected by criteria, sorting and Position.
Update — changes an item or moves it to another type.
DeleteItem — removes an item; acquire its lock first.
DeleteType — deletes the entire TDS type from the repository.
DeleteAll — deletes all repository contents; this operation cannot be cancelled.
LockItem / UnlockItem — explicitly manage an identified item's lock through its alias.
LockType / UnlockType — manage locks across a type.

elements.text: DeleteType removes one type and its records. DeleteAll wipes the whole repository — every type, every record. Don't reach for DeleteAll when only one type needs clearing.

bulletPoints: Find retrieves one item, not all matches. Position supports First, Random or a positive index; verify Start index and Sorting when choosing by index.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: ReadOnly does not reserve an item

elements.description: ReadOnly reads without acquiring an item lock. It is not the UnlockItem operation and should not be used to release a lock acquired earlier. Find reserves the retrieved item for exclusive use; documented automatic release occurs after execution or at a new loop iteration, including failure.

Use non-locking reads for shared reference values when the test does not require exclusive consumption. For example, several tests may read the same synthetic product-category record. Reading without reservation does not guarantee the data remains unchanged by other tests.

elements.text: Choose Find when the test needs an exclusive item. Use explicit UnlockItem when releasing a known lock; do not assume ReadOnly releases it.

bulletPoints: ReadOnly does not acquire an exclusive item lock.
Select a locking or non-locking operation according to the test's data ownership requirement.

elements.title: A practice workflow, not a verified Academy exercise
items: 1. Create a synthetic SampleOrders item with an OrderID and Pending status.
2. In a separate run, ReadOnly can inspect its attributes without reservation.
3. Find the intended item using an OrderID constraint and an alias.
4. Update its status through that alias.

elements.description: Set Create, type SampleOrders and alias order. Under Data structure, add OrderID and Status values with ActionMode Input. This creates an item containing those attributes.

Set ReadOnly and constrain OrderID to the intended item. Use Verify to check Status or buffer a value for later use. This read does not acquire a lock; it does not automatically unlock a previously reserved order.

bulletPoints: Reuse the module, but configure the task's type, alias, selection criteria and data actions at each TestStep.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing reading and unlocking
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting ReadOnly to reserve an item or release a lock held earlier.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: ReadOnly is non-locking. Use Find for reservation and UnlockItem for explicit release.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing DeleteType with DeleteAll
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Selecting DeleteAll when the intent was only to remove one TDS type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: DeleteType removes a single named type and its records. DeleteAll clears the entire repository — every type. Pick DeleteType for targeted cleanup.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting Find to return every matching record
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the Expert Module's Find task returns all records matching the criteria.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Find retrieves one selected item. Configure criteria, Sorting and Position rather than assuming First is the only supported selection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which listed Test data task reads an item without acquiring an exclusive lock?
practiceQuiz.hint: This one is designed for data meant to be shared, not consumed exclusively.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ReadOnly reads without acquiring a lock. It does not mean releasing an earlier lock or changing the item.

optionExplanations.A: Create adds an item rather than performing a non-locking read.
optionExplanations.B: Find reserves the retrieved item for exclusive use.
optionExplanations.C: ReadOnly retrieves data without reserving the item.
optionExplanations.D: Update changes an identified item rather than only reading it.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Several tests need to read the same synthetic product-category reference item without changing it or reserving it exclusively. Which task fits this requirement?
practiceQuiz.hint: The record needs to stay available to multiple testers at the same time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: ReadOnly meets the non-locking read requirement. It does not modify or delete reference data.

optionExplanations.A: DeleteItem removes data that the tests need to retain.
optionExplanations.B: Update changes data; the requirement is to read it.
optionExplanations.C: ReadOnly does not acquire an exclusive lock while reading.
optionExplanations.D: DeleteAll removes repository contents instead of reading reference data.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester wants to remove only the 'SampleOrders' TDS type and its records, leaving the rest of the repository untouched. Which Test data task should they use?
practiceQuiz.hint: One option wipes everything; another targets a single record; only one removes a whole type without touching the rest.
practiceQuiz.rationale: DeleteType removes the specified type and its items. DeleteAll affects the repository, while DeleteItem targets one item.

optionExplanations.A: DeleteAll also removes data outside SampleOrders.
optionExplanations.B: DeleteType matches the requested type-level scope.
optionExplanations.C: DeleteItem targets one item, not its entire type.
optionExplanations.D: ReadOnly reads data and does not remove the type.

quickRecap.value: One module for item operations, non-locking reads, type/repository deletion and explicit lock management.
Create, ReadOnly, Find, Update, DeleteItem, DeleteType, DeleteAll, LockItem, UnlockItem, LockType, UnlockType (2026.1 LTS).
Retrieves one item using criteria, sorting and Position (First, Random or index).
Reads without acquiring an item lock; not an automatic UnlockItem.
DeleteType = one type. DeleteAll = the whole repository.
